transcript:
This is NPR News now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says the Trump administration has warned it could
cut off intelligent sharing unless Ukraine stops long-range drone strikes on Russian
oil refineries.
And in an interview with NPR, Zelensky said President Trump's decision to lift sanctions
on Russian diesel will not bring down fuel prices.
"Mostly people in the world know why the prices on any kind of energy, including diesel,
raised up, why they increased because of hormones, because of blocking the straight of hormones.
Everybody understands that."
President Trump has blamed Ukraine for rising diesel prices, but Zelensky said Ukraine will
not stop strikes on Russian oil facilities unless Russia stops attacking Ukraine's energy
grid.
President Trump's ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, has resigned amid reports of misconduct.
She says she will defend herself, and she thanked Trump for what she called "in honor
of a lifetime," as St. Pierre's Michelle Kellerman reports.
President Trump says he didn't even talk to Guilfoyle, who was once engaged to his eldest
son.
"I don't think you'll know, but she will not be there.
I didn't like what I read."
Guilfoyle faces numerous allegations, including that she urged a Trump donor to pay off a
$100,000 credit card bill in exchange for access to the administration.
She says she will vigorously defend her name and reputation.
The ranking Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Gregory Meeks, is calling
for continued investigations, saying, quote, "Serving as a U.S. ambassador is a position
of public trust, not a business opportunity."
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department.
Cornell University is suspending parties and other social events at fraternity houses for
the rest of the academic year.
That announcement Tuesday comes amid outrage over the school's handling of gang rape allegations
in 2024.
In a letter to the campus, President Michael Kotlikoff said the university also plans to
allow for independent criminal investigators and add a case manager to help students navigate
reporting sexual misconduct.
New research from the AI company Anthropik suggested some AI might soon be able to replicate
inside smart devices.
Here's NPR's Jeff Brumfield.
Anthropik warned that AI models could soon spread inside network devices around the house,
including smart refrigerators, televisions, and even robotic vacuum cleaners.
Researchers demonstrated such replication inside some cheap TV boxes and with simulations.
The researchers warned AI worms would be similar to existing computer viruses, but they would
be more adaptable and could be hard to shut down.
The best defense against AI and regular viruses alike?
A strong password for every smart device in your home.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
This is NPR.
President Trump is to spend the night in Las Vegas after speaking at a campaign rally in
Alaska where he was stomping for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.
Speaking in Mozilla, Trump's remarks lasted nearly 90 minutes during his speech.
The president announced that Taiwan has agreed to buy 30 percent of the gas from a pipeline
project in Alaska.
The terms of the deal are not clear.
White evangelicals are the only group of registered voters in which a majority prefer GOP House
candidates for the midterm elections.
NPR's Jason Derose reports on the new findings by Pew Research.
Nearly three quarters of white evangelical Protestants expect to vote for their congressional
district's Republican candidate.
Pew Research also found white Catholic voters favor Republicans, though by a much narrower
margin.
Those more likely to support Democrats include black Protestants, Hispanic Catholics, atheists,
agnostics, and those who describe their religion as nothing in particular.
Regarding President Trump, white evangelical Protestants are the only religious group in
which a majority now approves of his job performance.
However, Pew found that approval has dropped by 20 points since his return to office.
Jason Derose, NPR News.
The Vatican says Pope Leo has lung cancer.
The Vatican made that announcement after Leo's surgery Tuesday, confirmed that cancer diagnosis.
He had the lower lobe of his right lung removed during a surgery that lasted about 90 minutes.
The Vatican says Leo returned afterward to his room at Rome's Jamali Hospital.
Oncologists say Leo's prognosis is excellent since it was discovered early.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.
This message comes from Cure Alzheimer's Fund.
From family to community, connections and the memories they make are everything.
Cure Alzheimer's Fund empowers scientists pursuing bold Alzheimer's research.
Learn more at curealz.org.

topics.text: Zelensky says US warned intelligence sharing could be cut unless Ukraine halts refinery strikes
Zelensky tells NPR Trump's Russian diesel sanctions lifting won't lower fuel prices
Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle resigns amid reports of misconduct allegations
Cornell suspends fraternity house parties for rest of academic year after gang rape handling outrage
Anthropic research warns AI models could spread across smart home devices like TVs and vacuums
Trump spends night in Las Vegas after Alaska rally backing Senator Dan Sullivan
Pew survey finds white evangelical voters strongly favor Republican House candidates in midterms
Vatican confirms Pope Leo has lung cancer after surgery removing lower right lung lobe
